'''Serge Alexandre Massar''' (born 11 February 1970)<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Massar |first=Serge Alexandre |date=March 2022 |title=CURRICULUM VITAE |url=https://liq.ulb.ac.be/docs/CV-short-March2022.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230807194919/https://liq.ulb.ac.be/docs/CV-short-March2022.pdf |archive-date=7 August 2023 |access-date=7 August 2023 |website=Laboratoire d'Information Quantique}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Serge Massar |url=https://liq.ulb.ac.be/serge_massar/ |access-date=2023-08-05 |website=Laboratoire d'Information Quantique |publisher=[[Université libre de Bruxelles]] |archive-date=2023-06-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230603114700/https://liq.ulb.ac.be/serge_massar/ |url-status=live }}</ref> is a Belgian physicist. He studies [[quantum information theory]], [[nonlinear optics]], [[optical neural network]]s, and [[reservoir computing]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />

==Early life and education==
Serge Massar was born in [[Zambia]] in 1970.<ref name=":0" /> He obtained a degree in [[physics]], then a PhD under the direction of [[Robert Brout]] from the [[Université libre de Bruxelles]] (ULB) in 1991 and 1995, respectively.<ref name=":0" /> He completed his post-doctoral research at [[Tel Aviv University]] from 1995 to 1997, and subsequently at [[Utrecht University]] from 1997 to 1998.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Physics - Serge Massar |url=https://physics.aps.org/authors/serge_massar |access-date=2023-08-05 |website=physics.aps.org |language=en |archive-date=2012-06-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120601191441/http://physics.aps.org/authors/serge_massar |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Career==
In 1998, Massar returned to ULB as a Research Associate of the [[FRS-FNRS]].<ref name=":0" /> In 2008 he became the Research Director of the [[FRS-FNRS]].<ref name=":0" />

In 2012, Massar integrated into the ULB faculty, holding the rank of "Professeur Ordinaire." His tenure as the Physics Department Director at ULB spanned 2014 to 2015.<ref name=":0" /> Additionally, he has been at the head of the Laboratoire d’Information Quantique at ULB since 2004.<ref name=":0" />

==Recognition==
Massar's recognition in the field includes awards such as the 2003 Alcatel-Bell Prize, the 2010 La Recherche Prize, and the best paper award at the [[Symposium on Theory of Computing]] in 2012.<ref name=":0" />

He has been a member of the [[Royal Academy of Science, Letters and Fine Arts of Belgium|Royal Academy of Science, Letters, and Fine Arts of Belgium]] since 2021.<ref name=":1" />

In 2023, he received the [[Gödel Prize]] for research on [[extension complexity]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The 2023 Gödel Prize |url=https://eatcs.org/index.php/component/content/article/1-news/2945-2023-05-18-18-41-48 |access-date=2023-08-04 |website=[[European Association for Theoretical Computer Science]] |archive-date=2023-06-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230622143014/https://eatcs.org/index.php/component/content/article/1-news/2945-2023-05-18-18-41-48 |url-status=live }}</ref>
